issues.description: The problem statement and UML clearly define an interface named 'Rideable' (with method messageOnRide()). The template/Main.java also uses 'Rideable'. However, the solution repository does not implement this interface: it provides an empty Rideable.java and instead introduces a different interface named 'Mountable' which Pig and Seal implement. This name/type mismatch between 'Rideable' and 'Mountable' is structural and will confuse students about which interface to implement and which types to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Either (a) rename Mountable to Rideable in the solution and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable (and populate Rideable.java accordingly), or (b) update the problem statement and template to use 'Mountable' instead of 'Rideable'. Ensure Rideable (or Mountable) declares messageOnRide() so students know the correct interface to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Rideable' with method messageOnRide(), but the solution introduces a different interface name 'Mountable' and has classes (Pig, Seal) implement Mountable. Additionally, the solution contains a Rideable.java file that is effectively empty. This inconsistent naming of the same conceptual interface (rideable/rideable-capability) across artifacts will confuse students mapping the UML/problem requirements to the provided code and reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Replace 'Mountable' in the solution with the expected 'Rideable' (define Rideable.java with messageOnRide()), and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable. Remove or populate the empty Rideable.java consistently so the template, problem statement, and solution all reference the same interface identifier.
